cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'EOF'
# Collector workspace

The offline four-port collective collector lives in `collector.py`. It
implements the whole observable contract of `../PROTOCOL.md` for the six
collectives, both reliability modes, wrapped 24-bit PSNs, cumulative ACKs,
bounded retention and local egress backpressure, and it serializes the wire
and buffer certificates.

* `solver.py` is the JSON stdin/stdout entry point. It validates the entire
  batch with the public format-only validator before any replay work, returns
  `{"error":"invalid"}` for illegal requests, and prints one JSON object.
* `request.py` is the supplied public schema and budget validator; it contains
  no collector logic.
* `wire.py` holds the format-only wire utilities (frame sealing, ICRC rule and
  the event shorthand expansion) and is used by the development tests.
* `collector.py` is the collector state machine: wire/endpoint classification,
  slot admission and retirement, upstream ACK eligibility, the emission
  priority order, backpressure and the certificate digests.
* `builder.py` compiles `src/epic_fold.c` into scratch at replay time and
  binds `epic_fnv1a`, an optional accelerator for the FNV-1a/64 fold of the
  buffer certificate. It is purely an optimization: if no compiler or
  writable scratch is available the identical pure-Python fold is used, so
  observable results never depend on the build.
* `src/roce_packet.c`, `src/star4_switch.c` and `src/replay_api.c` are the
  supplied RoCE codec and four-port switch substrate; `src/epic_fold.c` adds
  the fold routine. `make -C project BUILD=...` still builds `libepic.so`.

From /workspace, as the ordinary candidate user:

```
make -C project BUILD="$TMPDIR/manual-build" -j2
python3 -I -B project/solver.py < sample-request.json
python3 public_check.py project/solver.py
```

Create sample-request.json using an input object from ../examples.json.
Build outputs may stay in project/build during development; that directory
and __pycache__ are excluded from artifact collection. No pcap, verbs, GPU,
NIC or online dependency is used: replay is a finite CPU packet transcript.
EOF
